GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm: the vulnerable code is launch-editor, which vite 5.4.21 bundles into its dist rather than resolving as a package — so it is absent from pnpm-lock.yaml while escapeCmdArgs, launchEditor and guessEditor are all present in dist/node/chunks/dep-BK3b2jBa.js, reachable through the dev server's __open-in-editor endpoint. Because the code is inlined, a pnpm override cannot substitute a patched launch-editor; the fix for the 5.x line is vite 6.4.4, gated on vitepress 2.x. Accepted rather than dismissed: exposure requires a developer to be running 'vitepress dev' locally, all three vectors are Windows-specific, vite 5.4.21 reaches this repo only as a transitive dev dependency of the documentation site (the prod audit is clean), and the workspace's other vite is 8.3.4, above the 8.3.3 fix. Revisit when vitepress 2.x lands (hdf-libs-34nl).

GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw: cross-origin script execution through Vite custom middleware — a malicious site visited WHILE the dev server runs can load scripts in a page the dev server serves. CVSS 4.0 records UI:A and AT:P, so it needs the developer to visit the hostile page and the app to pass an unchanged browser request URL to server.transformIndexHtml; whether vitepress does that is NOT established here, so this waiver does not rest on it. Exposure requires a developer to be running 'vitepress dev' locally: vite 5.4.21 reaches this repo only as a transitive dev dependency of the documentation site, which is not a published package, and the prod audit is clean. No 5.x fix exists — 5.4.21 is the last 5.x and the fix line starts at 6.4.4 — so it clears with the vitepress 2.x bump (hdf-libs-34nl). The workspace's other vite is 8.3.4, above the 8.3.3 fix.

GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4: glob 13.0.6 keeps reading directories after its AbortSignal fires, so a caller that passes signal or AbortSignal.timeout() to bound a walk still pays the I/O. The vulnerable branch is only entered when a signal is supplied. glob reaches this repo solely through rimraf 6.1.3 (dev), whose only use is the per-package 'clean' scripts invoking the rimraf CLI on literal paths; the CLI exposes no signal option and rimraf forwards one to glob only when its caller supplies it, so the abort branch is never taken. 'pnpm why -r --prod glob' returns no paths. The fix (14.0.2) is a new major published 2026-10-27 that also pulls in a path-scurry major and a brand-new package, all inside the seven-day release cooldown; it is taken once they clear the cooldown, and this waiver goes with it.

GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249: minimatch below 11.0.1 lets an attacker-controlled glob pattern amplify globParts in firstPhasePreProcess and then pay quadratic pairwise work, so it is a CPU/memory denial of service against whoever compiles the pattern. Every minimatch in this tree is dev (3.1.4 under eslint 8 via the SARIF formatter, 5.1.9 under @redocly/openapi-core, 10.2.3 under stryker, 10.2.6 under eslint 10 and typescript-eslint); 'pnpm why -r --prod minimatch' returns no paths. Every pattern those consumers compile comes from checked-in configuration (eslint ignore globs, stryker mutate globs, the OpenAPI tooling config), none from input a third party supplies, so the precondition is not met. The only fix (11.0.1) is a new major published 2026-10-27 that depends on a brand-new package, both inside the seven-day release cooldown; it is taken once they clear the cooldown, and this adjustment goes with it.
